article.title: Oleshky evacuation begins as former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine calls Vladimir Putin an “obstacle” to talks
paras: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Russian article.

A large evacuation and humanitarian mission is currently under way in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky on the Dnipro River. The temporary ceasefire that made the truce evacuation possible, brokered by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump, is a rare example of successful Russia-Ukraine negotiations. Speaking to VOA, a former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine says this temporary ceasefire is proof progress towards peace can be made.
On Friday morning, a delegation of Russian and Ukrainian human rights officials entered the war-ravaged town, and residents began boarding a convoy of buses to leave.

The convoy of about 25 buses arrived in Oleshky via Russian-occupied Crimea, about 85 km away. Ukraine’s ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said the road had to be demined before the buses could travel safely. Two people were killed during the demining according to Russia’s human rights commissioner, Yana Lantratova.

Residents of Oleshky can choose to go to Ukraine or Russia. Residents who choose to go to Ukraine will travel to Russia, then fly to Belarus before crossing into Ukraine. Others are choosing to stay in Russia. About 2 thousand people were living in Oleshky when the evacuation was announced. Over 500 evacuees are choosing to relocate to Ukraine.

William B. Taylor, an expert at the Atlantic Council who served as U.S. Ambassador (2006-2009) and later as Chargé d’Affaires (2019–2020) in Ukraine, spoke to the VOA Russian Service about the prospects for the temporary ceasefire in Oleshky and its potential impact on U.S. President Donald Trump’s planned trilateral talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States.

According to Ambassador Taylor, the situation in Oleshky was horrific, and many people around the world, particularly Ukrainians, have been making the case that this horrible humanitarian situation needs to be addressed.
The city has been under constant shelling, and the residents who remain there have been left without drinking water or food. The routes out of the city have been mined.

Eventually, Taylor said, high profile figures such as Pope Leo XIV, the White House and Melania Trump took notice: "They raised it to a higher level of attention, and put some pressure on Putin." On October 23, an agreement on a temporary, localized ceasefire around the city was announced.
While it is impossible to say for sure, he believed it forced Putin to agree to a ceasefire: "It looked so bad for the Russians that they had to act."
The ceasefire was initially scheduled to start on October 29, but it went into effect earlier, on October 27, and is expected to remain in place through November 1.

Regarding U.S. involvement, Taylor described the ceasefire agreement as long overdue: "This should have happened a long time ago. The delay only prolonged the suffering of Ukrainians living in Russian-controlled territories."

According to Taylor, it is yet unknown whether this localized ceasefire could affect the upcoming scheduled trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine and U.S., either at the technical level or at the summit level. The experience with prisoner exchanges and the P.O.W. exchanges between Russian and Ukraine demonstrate that progress can be achieved: "It shows that it's possible for the Ukrainians and the Russians to have an agreement, having a talk come to some understanding about how things can work. And that may be a good signal."
Taylor pointed that the Ukrainians have made it very clear that they're willing to talk and have already made some compromises, for example, about freezing the front lines.

"Many people, many Ukrainians want to push the Russians all the way out of their country back to 1991 borders. So, the point is, the Ukrainians have already made compromises. The Ukrainians have already proposed ceasefires. The Ukrainians have agreed with Trump on an energy cease fire."
The single obstacle for a successful trilateral meeting is the president of Russia: "There's one obstacle. There's just one obstacle, and that's Vladimir Putin," said Taylor.
zh: 奧列什基撤離行動展開，前美國駐烏克蘭大使稱弗拉基米爾·普京是談判的「障礙」
編者註：本報導翻譯自美國之音（VOA）俄語原文。
目前，在第聶伯河畔、由俄羅斯佔領的烏克蘭城市奧列什基，一項大規模的撤離與人道主義行動正在進行中。這項撤離行動得以實現，是因美國第一夫人梅拉尼婭·川普斡旋促成的臨時停火所致，這可說是俄烏談判中難得的成功案例。 一位前美國駐烏克蘭大使在接受美國之音（VOA）採訪時表示，這項臨時停火證明了朝著和平邁進是可行的。
週五上午，一支由俄羅斯和烏克蘭人權官員組成的代表團進入了這座飽受戰火蹂躪的小鎮，居民們開始登上巴士車隊準備撤離。
這支由約25輛巴士組成的車隊，經由距離約85公里的俄羅斯佔領的克里米亞，抵達奧列什基。烏克蘭人權專員德米特羅·盧比涅茨表示，必須先對道路進行排雷，巴士才能安全通行。 據俄羅斯人權專員雅娜·蘭特拉托娃稱，在排雷過程中有兩人喪生。
奧列什基的居民可以選擇前往烏克蘭或俄羅斯。 選擇前往烏克蘭的居民將先前往俄羅斯，再飛往白俄羅斯，最後進入烏克蘭。其他人則選擇留在俄羅斯。在宣布疏散時，奧列什基約有 2,000 名居民。目前已有超過 500 名疏散民眾選擇遷往烏克蘭。
大西洋理事會專家威廉·B·泰勒（William B. Taylor）曾於2006至2009年間擔任美國駐烏克蘭大使，其後於 （2019–2020年），接受美國之音俄語組採訪時，談及奧列什基地區臨時停火的前景，以及這對美國總統唐納德·川普計劃中由俄羅斯、烏克蘭和美國參與的三方會談可能產生的影響。
據泰勒大使表示，奧列什基的局勢極為駭人，世界各地許多人，尤其是烏克蘭人，一直主張必須解決這場可怕的人道主義危機。
這座城市一直遭受持續的砲擊，仍留在當地的居民已無飲用水和食物。通往城外的道路上都埋設了地雷。
泰勒表示，最終，教宗利奧十四世、白宮以及梅拉尼婭·川普等備受矚目的人物都注意到了此事：「他們將此事提升到更高的關注層級，並對普丁施加了一定壓力。」10月23日，當局宣布達成一項協議，將在該市周邊實施臨時且局部的停火。
雖然無法斷言，但他認為這迫使普丁同意停火：「俄方處境看起來如此糟糕，以致他們不得不採取行動。」
停火原本定於10月29日開始，但實際上已提前於10月27日生效，預計將持續至11月1日。
關於美國的介入，泰勒表示這項停火協議早該達成：「這本該在很久以前就實現。延宕只會延長生活在俄羅斯控制區內的烏克蘭人的苦難。」
泰勒表示，目前尚不清楚這項局部停火是否會影響俄羅斯、烏克蘭與美國之間即將舉行的三方會談，無論是技術層級還是峰會層級的會談。 俄烏雙方在戰俘交換方面的經驗表明，雙方確實能夠取得進展：「這顯示烏克蘭與俄羅斯有能力達成協議，透過對話就事態如何發展達成某種共識。這或許是個好訊號。」
泰勒指出，烏克蘭方面已非常明確地表示願意進行談判，並且已經做出了一些讓步，例如關於凍結前線的提議。
「許多人，許多烏克蘭人希望將俄羅斯人徹底趕出他們的國家，退回1991年的邊界。所以，重點在於，烏克蘭人已經做出讓步。烏克蘭人已經提出停火建議。烏克蘭人還與川普就能源停火達成共識。」
三方會談能否成功，唯一的障礙就是俄羅斯總統：「只有一個障礙。只有一個障礙，那就是弗拉基米爾·普京，」泰勒表示。
